PRE-DRAFT — The two comparisons for the 2027 Glean-history forecast

The locked 2027 forecast (world MAU 2027-12-15 157,222,571) is trained on a simulated Glean history: Legacy telemetry restated the way Glean counts. Two comparisons test that choice, both with the identical locked configuration (g01 lock, changepoint range 0.87, Iran fill, 2025 outage calendar, China correction) and the identical seam 2026-10-10:

  1. Legacy telemetry (2020-01-01 → 2026-10-09) — the data the simulated history was made from. If the model is doing the same thing on both, the two forecasts should differ by the translation factor and nothing else.
  2. Real Glean telemetry, no simulated history (2025-05-22 → 2026-10-09, 17 months) — the data we actually have. Expected to be poor, required anyway.

1. Legacy MAU and DAU — same model, Legacy telemetry

Result: the two forecasts are the same forecast in different units. Glean-equivalent ÷ Legacy world MAU is 1.032 in the last weeks of history and 1.030 at 2027-12-15; Dec → Dec is -1.9% on Legacy and -1.9% on Glean-equivalent. The same holds per OS (Linux's larger factor, 1.145, carries through unchanged). The simulated history changes what the numbers mean, not what the model does.

The ratio of the two, through the horizon. Solid is history (Glean-equivalent ÷ Legacy actuals), dashed is forecast ÷ forecast. A flat dashed line continuing the solid one is what "translation-invariant" looks like; Mac's small drift (0.987 → 0.999 in MAU) is the one place the two forecasts diverge, and it is 1.2% on an 11.7M series.

2. Real Glean MAU and DAU — same model, real Glean only, no simulated history

Result: unusable, as expected. With 17 months of history the model's "forecast" takes world MAU from 169,179,300 on 2026-10-09 to 228,835,354 on 2027-12-15 (+46% over the locked forecast); Windows DAU goes negative; Linux MAU goes negative. These are not forecasts of anything. The page shows them because they are what the real data, treated the same way, produces.

Why it fails (three reasons, in order of size)

  1. One autumn, seen once. Prophet needs at least two passes through a season to separate yearly seasonality from trend. The only autumn ramp this run saw (Aug–Oct 2026, +12% in world MAU) is read as trend and extrapolated for 15 months. The backtest of the locked configuration said the same thing: seams with under four years of history missed by 30–90% at 14 months (backtest_round1/), which is why the stated error band uses only seams with ≥ 4 years.
  2. The run masked three months it should not have. The LegacyOutage2025 holiday calendar (Windows 2025-08-16 → 11-06, Mac 08-28 → 12-10, applied as one union window) is wired into the runner unconditionally because every Glean-history input inherits the Legacy outage. Real Glean has no outage in that window (the black line in the shaded region is clean), so the mask threw away the first autumn too, leaving the model with no 2025 autumn at all. This is a defect of the run as executed, separate from the short-history problem; fixing it needs a runner flag and a one-minute rerun.
  3. The Iran fill is in Glean-equivalent units (the locked build's fill was passed through). Real Glean ÷ Glean-equivalent is within ±1% on DAU, so this is small, but a clean run would regenerate the fill from the real-Glean frames.

Does a shorter horizon help? No — it is already wrong at one month

The real-Glean-only build against the locked one, world, by horizon (csv/glean2027_vs_glean_real_comparison.csv). The last column is the build against its own last actual, so no translation question enters: world MAU is +8% above its own October level after one month, in a season where the locked build and every prior year flatten. The trend misread happens at the seam, not at the horizon, so cutting the horizon only hides it.

What the real data does tell us: the units

Over the 17-month overlap, real Glean ÷ Glean-equivalent (csv/glean2027_in_real_glean_units.csv, plot below) is the part of real Glean the glean_equivalent column deliberately excludes: the pre-Fx-148 duplicate-id MAU inflation (world MAU ratio 1.077 in mid-2025, falling to ~1.02 by spring 2026 as Fx 148+ rolled out) and the Linux Glean-only temporary term (Linux MAU ratio 1.40 at the seam, still rising). DAU is within 1% throughout. These are the two combinatorics candidates registered in adjustments/ (d, x), measured.

It is the honest answer to "what would the real Glean MAU number read on 2027-12-15": world 163,477,422 rather than 157,222,571, if nothing about the two excluded terms changes.

3. Options for the real-Glean comparison — for decision, nothing run

Recommendation: do (a), present (c) beside it, and record (b) and (d) as not informative. (a) is a model run and waits for the word.
optionwhatneeds a model run?expected outcome
(a) Rerun real Glean without the outage mask, with a real-Glean Iran fillAdd a --no-outage-calendar flag to the runner; regenerate the fill from raw_glean_real_osxcountry_2026-10-09/; same configuration otherwise.Yes (~1 min)Still not usable at 14 months — reason 1 stands — but the run is then a fair statement of what the real data gives, with no treatment designed for the simulated history left in it. Worth doing for the record.
(b) Shorter horizonReport the real-Glean-only build to, say, 2027-01 or 2027-03 only.NoNot informative: the table above shows the build is already +15% over the locked forecast at one month. The error is a trend misread at the seam.
(c) Restate the locked forecast in real-Glean unitsLocked forecast × the seam-time real ÷ Glean-equivalent ratio per OS and metric (the table above; already written).No Informative as a reading aid, not as a forecast: it says what the dashboard would show on 2027-12-15 if the duplicate-id and Linux terms stayed where they are. Could be shown beside the headline with that caveat.
(d) Real Glean trend + seasonality borrowed from LegacyFit the level/trend on real Glean, take yearly seasonality and holidays from the Legacy (or Glean-equivalent) tiles. Yes, plus mozaic codeThis is the simulated-history approach by another route: the seasonality would come from the same Legacy data. It would not be an independent check.
